name: cyberchef
one_line: the 'Cyber Swiss Army Knife' for encoding, decoding and data analysis
plain: CyberChef is a web page (it also works offline from one HTML file) that converts and analyses data by chaining small operations. You drag operations into a recipe (From Base64, then Gunzip, then XOR...) and the output updates as you build.
It is the fastest way to decode a mystery string in a CTF: Base64, hex, URL encoding, ROT13, XOR, hashing, compression, regular expressions, file type detection, and many more.

The page has four areas: Operations (left, searchable), Recipe (the chain), Input and Output. Because it runs entirely in the browser, your data does not leave your machine when you use the offline copy.
when: Chain several decodings (Base64 then hex then gzip).
Try XOR with a key or brute-force a single-byte key.
Extract IPs, URLs, emails or flags with a regex.
Hash or encrypt a value, or find the file type of a blob.

examples.title: Decode Base64
examples.cmd: Search 'From Base64', drag it into the Recipe, paste the text in Input
examples.explain: The decoded text appears in Output. If it is still garbled, add another operation after it.

examples.title: Let Magic guess
examples.explain: Magic tries many decoders and shows the ones that produce readable text. Raise the depth to try chains. A superb first move on an unknown blob.

examples.title: Chain operations
examples.explain: Operations run top to bottom. Use the disable and breakpoint icons to debug a chain.

examples.title: XOR with a key
examples.cmd: XOR with Key 'k' (UTF8)    or    XOR Brute Force
examples.explain: XOR Brute Force tries every single-byte key and lets you grep the results for known text (crib) such as 'flag'.

examples.title: Extract with a regex
examples.cmd: Regular expression > Output format: List matches   (pattern: flag\{.*?\})
examples.explain: Pulls every match out of a large input. Use 'Extract IP addresses' or 'Extract URLs' for common cases.

examples.title: Identify a file
examples.cmd: Detect File Type    or    Extract Files
examples.explain: Finds magic bytes and can carve out embedded files; the output can be downloaded.

examples.title: Hash a value
examples.explain: Quick checks of a hash against what you have.

examples.title: Save and share a recipe
examples.cmd: Save recipe icon > Chef format / Deep link
examples.explain: A deep link contains your recipe in the URL after #, so you can bookmark or share a decode chain without the data.

examples.title: Work from a file
examples.cmd: Open file as input icon (top of Input)
examples.explain: Loads a binary directly; Output has Save to file.

mistakes: Pasting binary data into the Input and having it altered by character encoding: use 'Open file as input' for binaries.
Wrong order of operations: always decode in the reverse of how it was encoded.
Trusting Magic blindly: check the output makes sense.
Using the online site for secrets: use the offline copy.
Forgetting that Output replaced Input: use the 'replace input' button deliberately.
try: Use Magic on a string you do not recognise.
Build From Base64 > From Hex > Gunzip for a nested test string you make yourself.
Run XOR Brute Force and search for 'flag'.
